subsections.content: In Shenyang, the lowest temperature on a particular day was -12°C, or 12 degrees below zero. This introduces negative numbers. Negative numbers are useful for describing quantities below a reference point, as well as many other opposite quantities. They extend the number system and make it more useful.

Suppose the same day had a high of 3°C and a low of -12°C. These temperatures lie on opposite sides of zero, so we can represent them with positive and negative numbers. Many everyday quantities have opposites that can be described this way.

For example, if east is positive, traveling 3.5 km east is recorded as 3.5 km and traveling 2.5 km west as -2.5 km. If income is positive, income of 500 yuan is recorded as 500 yuan and an expense of 237 yuan as -237 yuan. If a rise in water level is positive, a rise of 1.2 m is 1.2 m and a fall of 0.7 m is -0.7 m.

Numbers such as -12, -2.5, -237, and -0.7 are negative numbers; 3, 3.5, 500, and 1.2 are positive numbers. A positive number may be written with a plus sign, so 7 may also be written as +7. Zero is neither positive nor negative.

The numbers studied so far include positive integers such as 1, 2, 3, …; zero; negative integers such as -1, -2, -3, …; positive fractions such as 1/3 and 22/7; and negative fractions such as -1/2 and -2 2/7. Integers and fractions together are called rational numbers. Every rational number can be written as a ratio of two integers with a nonzero denominator.
The word rational is related to ratio: a rational number can be expressed as a ratio of integers. This description captures the defining property of rational numbers.

A collection of numbers is called a set. The set of all rational numbers is the set of rational numbers; similarly, we can define the set of integers, the set of negative numbers, and the set of nonnegative integers (the natural numbers, including zero).
Classify each number into every set to which it belongs: -18, 3.1416, 0, 2023, -0.142857, and 95%. Explain your choices.
